title: Sell Mineral Rights in Gilcrest, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Gilcrest, CO | Weld County DJ Basin
metaDescription: Own minerals near Gilcrest in the Wattenberg field? Get a direct offer priced off your decline curve and recent comparable sales.
heroLead: Two numbers drive nearly every mineral offer we make near Gilcrest: your net revenue interest and how far along the decline curve your unit currently sits.
intro: This stretch of Weld County along the South Platte River has seen sustained horizontal drilling for over a decade, so most Gilcrest-area interests we evaluate come with an established check-stub history rather than starting from scratch on comparables.

We start every offer the same way here: confirm the net revenue interest from your division order, pull trailing production, fit a decline curve, and check that number against recent comparable sales in this part of Weld County before finalizing a price.

sections.heading: Why decline curve matters more than county reputation
paragraphs: Two Gilcrest-area interests with identical net revenue interests can price very differently depending on well age. A well in year two of production still has most of its economic life ahead of it; a well in year ten is mostly on the flat tail. We price the actual curve, not a generic assumption.

sections.heading: River-corridor surface considerations
paragraphs: Acreage along the South Platte corridor sometimes has floodplain or setback considerations that affect where new wells can be sited, though this mainly matters for undeveloped acreage rather than interests already inside a producing unit.

sections.heading: Recent comparable activity
paragraphs: We track recent mineral sales across this stretch of Weld County and use them as a sanity check against our decline-curve pricing, so the number we offer reflects both your specific production history and what the broader market is doing right now.

sections.heading: What floodplain notes on a deed mean
paragraphs: Some Gilcrest-area parcels near the South Platte carry floodplain notations on the surface deed. These do not affect your mineral ownership or its value directly, but they can factor into where a future operator sites a well on undeveloped acreage, which we account for when pricing unleased tracts.

faqs.question: What is the single most important document for pricing?
faqs.answer: Your division order, since it establishes your exact net revenue interest across every unit your tract touches.

faqs.question: Does river-adjacent land affect my offer?
faqs.answer: Mainly for undeveloped acreage, where floodplain considerations can affect siting. Producing interests price off decline curve regardless.

faqs.question: How do you make sure your offer is competitive?
faqs.answer: We check decline-curve pricing against recent comparable Weld County sales before finalizing a number.

faqs.question: Does a floodplain note on my deed affect my mineral rights value?
faqs.answer: Not directly for producing interests. For undeveloped acreage it can factor into siting considerations, which we weigh when pricing.
